field.label: Description
field.help: You may enter a description here for your reference (not parsed).

field.label: Use these common settings
field.help: Common settings for the physical device, the ones marked will be used.

field.label: Minimum standard
field.help: When operating as an access point, allow only stations capable of the selected wireless standard to associate (stations not capable are not permitted to associate).

field.label: 802.11g OFDM Protection Mode
field.help: For IEEE 802.11g, use the specified technique for protecting OFDM frames in a mixed 11b/11g network.

field.label: Transmit power
field.help: Typically only a few discreet power settings are available and the driver will use the setting closest to the specified value. Not all adapters support changing the transmit power setting.

field.label: Channel
field.help: Not all channels may be supported by your card.

field.label: Transmit antenna
field.help: Note: The antenna numbers do not always match up with the labels on the card.

field.label: Receive antenna
field.help: Note: The antenna numbers do not always match up with the labels on the card.

field.label: Regulatory domain
field.help: Some cards have a default that is not recognized and require changing the regulatory domain to one in this list for the changes to other regulatory settings to work.

field.label: Country
field.help: Any country setting other than "Default" will override the regulatory domain setting.

field.label: Location
field.help: These settings may affect which channels are available and the maximum transmit power allowed on those channels. Using the correct settings to comply with local regulatory requirements is recommended. All wireless networks on this interface will be temporarily brought down when changing regulatory settings. Some of the regulatory domains or country codes may not be allowed by some cards. These settings may not be able to add additional channels that are not already supported.

field.label: SSID
field.help: Note: Only required in Access Point mode. If left blank in Ad-hoc or Infrastructure mode, this interface will connect to any available SSID

field.label: Pure 802.11g mode
field.help: When operating as an access point, allow only stations capable of the selected wireless standard to associate (stations not capable are not permitted to associate).

field.label: Pure 802.11n mode
field.help: When operating as an access point, allow only stations capable of the selected wireless standard to associate (stations not capable are not permitted to associate).

field.label: Allow intra-BSS communication
field.help: When operating as an access point, enable this if you want to pass packets between wireless clients directly.

field.label: Enable WME
field.help: Setting this option will force the card to use WME (wireless QoS).

field.label: Enable Hide SSID
field.help: Setting this option will force the card to NOT broadcast its SSID (this might create problems for some clients).

field.label: WEP key
field.help:
40 (64) bit keys may be entered as 5 ASCII characters or 10 hex digits preceded by '0x'.
104 (128) bit keys may be entered as 13 ASCII characters or 26 hex digits preceded by '0x'.
Maximum 4 keys, preferred key first.

field.label: WPA EAP Identity
field.help: Only relevant when Extended Authentication Protocol (EAP) is used.

field.label: WPA Pre-Shared Key/EAP Password
field.help: Passphrase must be from 8 to 63 characters.

field.label: EAP Method
field.help: Note: Only relevant for infrastructure mode (BSS) and if Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is used for key management.

field.label: EAP Phase 2 Authentication
field.help: Note: Only relevant for infrastructure mode (BSS) and if Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is used for key management.

field.label: EAP TLS CA Certificate
field.help: Certificate authority used to verify the access point\'s TLS certificate. Only relevant for infrastructure mode (BSS) if Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is used for key management.

field.label: EAP TLS Client Certificate
field.help: Certificate used for authentication towards the access point. Only relevant for infrastructure mode (BSS) if EAP with TLS is used for key management.

field.label: Access Point Authentication
field.help: Note: Shared Key Authentication requires WEP. Only relevant for access point mode.

field.label: Key Rotation
field.help: Allowed values are 1-9999 but should not be longer than Master Key Regeneration time.

field.label: Master Key Regeneration
field.help: Allowed values are 1-9999 but should not be shorter than Key Rotation time.

field.label: Strict Key Regeneration
field.help: Setting this option will force the AP to rekey whenever a client disassociates.

field.label: Enable IEEE802.1X Authentication
field.help: This option requires checking the "Enable WPA box".

field.label: 802.1X Server IP Address
field.help: Enter the IP address of the 802.1X Authentication Server. This is commonly a Radius server (FreeRadius, Internet Authentication Services, etc.

field.label: 802.1X Server Port
field.help: Leave blank for the default 1812 port.

field.label: 802.1X Server IP Address (2)
field.help: Secondary 802.1X Authentication Server IP Address

field.label: 802.1X Server Port (2)
field.help: Secondary 802.1X Authentication Server Port

field.label: 802.1X Server Shared Secret (2)
field.help: Secondary 802.1X Authentication Server Shared Secret
